A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A–C are readable and matchable despite additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification evaluations, dynamical-system simulations, hippocampal-data analysis and MNIST experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of a simplex-based SSL variant.

M1.justification: Appendix A.6.1 adds a deterministic softmax/simplex variant with a Dirichlet conditional model and contrastive entropy objective. This differs from the probabilistic categorical model already present in A.8. The core LDM framework and Kalman filtering procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, ImageNet-100, MNIST, hippocampal spike trains and the same synthetic dynamical tasks. The simplex extension changes the representation model, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table A1 adds the evaluated Simplex–contrastive–MI variant to the existing plane/sphere comparison set. The VICReg and SimCLR reference variants remain. DINO is discussed as related work, rather than separately benchmarked.

E3.justification: The stated linear-probing metrics, data selections, training budgets and simulation procedures remain unchanged. The simplex results use the existing Table A1 evaluation setup; Appendix B reports no corresponding protocol revision.

E4.justification: The new simplex subsection reports that kNN and LogDet entropy estimators fail to converge, supplementing the successful contrastive variant with a limited estimator-suitability analysis. Existing gradient, noise-robustness and dimensionality analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table A1 retains standard deviations based on three runs, including for the added row. The five-run confidence intervals in Figure A7 and model-based uncertainty procedures are unchanged. No new statistical reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table A1 adds simplex Top-1 accuracies of 90.23±0.13, 62.65±0.22, 92.21±0.07 and 70.50 for CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and ImageNet-100, respectively, plus Top-5 results. Appendix A.6.1 also adds the nonconvergence finding for kNN and LogDet. Existing numerical rows and headline findings are retained.

T1.justification: v4 adds the simplex/Dirichlet derivation in Equations 49–51. It corrects Equation 15's Kalman residual to z_t - D A h_{t-1} and fixes the Gaussian objective's sign in v1 Equation 57, now Equation 60. The identifiability theorems and folding-entropy proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and discussion retain the same unification, MI, Kalman uncertainty and affine-identifiability claims. Section 7 emphasizes generality and conditional-only matching already explained in v1 Appendix A.7.1.

C2.justification: The simplex subsection explains its encodings as deterministic points and relates collapse prevention to contrastive entropy and normalization terms, contrasting this with DINO's heuristics. It also identifies an applicability limitation for kNN and LogDet on the simplex.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same implementation and hyperparameter disclosures. Its explicitly printed repository URL was already the target of v1's 'simulation code' hyperlink, so code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Caron et al. (2021) and connects the simplex objective to DINO. It also makes the relationship to existing identifiability and invertibility work more explicit in Section 7 and Appendix A.4.2, without substantially reorganizing related work.

P1.justification: Edits include rewriting Section 7's opening, adding the simplex subsection, replacing several uses of 'loss function' with 'goal function', simplifying notation and updating the publication footer. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table A1 gains one row, Table 2 moves from page 5 to page 6, and Figure 5 changes position within page 8. Other changes are limited to reflow and minor figure rendering adjustments; no substantive new figure is added.

improvement.justification: The derived and tested simplex example modestly extends the framework, while the Kalman residual and Gaussian-objective sign corrections improve mathematical consistency. Existing evidence and guarantees are retained. The gain is limited: the new KDE Equation 51 uses a Dirichlet parameter without the +1 required by its displayed expansion, leaving a small internal inconsistency.
